title: Retrospective data analysis on prediction, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of urological tumors
summary:
The study focuses on cancers of the urinary tract, such as those of the prostate, kidneys, and bladder. These diseases can progress in very different ways, which is why it is important to establish the most accurate diagnosis possible and find a treatment tailored to each individual.

To achieve this, existing patient data from routine clinical practice is used, such as personal information, test results, images (e.g., from scans), tissue samples, treatment histories, and medical reports. The goal is to use this wealth of information to better assess how a disease might progress and which treatment is most appropriate.

Modern computer algorithms capable of analyzing large amounts of data are used for this purpose. The goal is to identify patterns that help predict disease progression, such as whether a tumor will recur or whether side effects are likely. In the long term, this should allow treatment to be more closely tailored to the individual and improve quality of life.

The study uses only existing data from patient records. No additional examinations or appointments will take place. All data is protected and processed in such a way that no conclusions can be drawn about individual patients.

interventions.name: A retrospective analysis of patients with suspected or confirmed prostate, kidney, or urothelial carcinomas, or other diseases of these organs, who were treated between 2005 and 2025 at the university hospital Heidelberg

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with suspected or confirmed prostate, kidney, or urothelial carcinoma, or other diseases of the prostate, kidney, or bladder, who underwent a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure at the UKHD Department of Urology between January 2005 and December 2025
Exclusion criteria:
Patients under 18 years of age
